summary: Recheck of 3 closed or rejected ideas against the new facts (x138 base, 0.954 with insertion, ~4 h runtime headroom, ranking inside a displayed score by the unrounded score, public = 1 embryo and private = 71%). Round 1's lens_mine-old already covered the ideas rejected for runtime (simview-readmit, DoG, dense-dorado, third detector, two-tail, budget deadline), so they are not repeated here. (A) REVIVE, small: float output coordinates with the safe encoding (I-028) were closed as 'ties twice' on the OLD bases (P32/P33). They were never ported to x138, whose writer rounds z to the 1.625 um voxel grid. The patch is coordinate-only: on a rounding or truncating server it gives the same score by construction, and P32/P33 already showed there is no parse risk. Expected +0.0000..+0.0004. That was invisible under the old 'late-copy tie' framing. Now that ranks inside a block follow the unrounded score (~62 teams per 0.001 in the 0.954 block), it can matter. Cost ~1.5-2 agent-h to port (patch_floatout hardcodes cell 7; x138's writer is cell 5) plus a dummy check folded into K3/S12. It needs the user's OK as an R3 coordinate rider. (B) STAYS CLOSED: division-ADD ideas judged at the public break-even of 0.265 (mirror/lowdet daughter I-077, edge-evidence second daughter I-078). Two of the old premises changed. The '0.003 LB noise' premise was overturned, and an x138 lab (exp60) now exists. The private break-even (0.11-0.20) was already priced in by the v3 skeptics (private +0.0005 central, unverified). The inputs are in-sample on the lab clips, R4 cannot adopt a fork-set changer below +0.002 public, and R8 closes new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00. (C) STAYS DROPPED: tempfuse K4 (E7/C07). The runtime headroom is irrelevant (0 GPU). Detection-map changes went 0/5 on the LB. exp60 is in-sample for the detector. The R4 read has ~25% false adoption at a true 0. Its variance works against P(F1 > x138). The curator's default DROP should be confirmed before 26 Sep 12:00 UTC.

findings.what: Float output coordinates, safe encoding (I-028 / wf_ideas_v2 #1). OLD VERDICT: 'lb-tested, harmless but invisible'. Lab +0.0019 [+0.00115, +0.00271] on 199 videos, and e48 SELECTION +0.00248 [+0.00105, +0.0039] with 24 wins / 10 losses. LB: P32 exp52 0.950 = exp51 and P33 exp53 0.948 = exp48 (ties). Kept only inside exp52 (old F2); never ported to x138. WHAT CHANGED: (1) The base is now x138. Its writer does int(round(float(node['z']))), so the V1284 head's sub-voxel z (z = 66% of the error variance) and linefit/lowrefine float positions are quantised to 1.625 um in z on every node of K2/K3. (2) The v3 rationale for 'F1 must differ from x138' was about byte copies. Round 1 found that the order inside a displayed score follows the UNROUNDED score (0.954 block = ranks 134-195, ~62 teams per 0.001). A non-negative +0.0001..+0.0004 therefore buys ~6-25 private ranks near the silver edge (~195), where before it was 'invisible'. (3) The ~4 h runtime headroom does not matter: the cost is seconds. NEW VERDICT: REVIVE as a coordinate-only R3 rider on the F1 stack (K3 or the S12 consolidation), not on the exp58n twin, which keeps the twin a one-difference hedge. With the safe encoding, floor(w) == round(v): a rounding or int-casting server scores byte-identically, and a Float64 server (royerlab csv_to_geffs.py casts z/y/x to Float64 without rounding) gets the float values. The two LB ties bound the float-server gain at < ~0.0005, so E ~ +0.0000..+0.0004 and P(harm) is small; parse risk was already retired by P32/P33. Caveat: GT centroids are integer voxels, so rounding can snap accurate z onto the GT grid, and the lab's float advantage is partly in-sample.

findings.what: Division-ADD ideas rejected against the PUBLIC break-even J/(1+J) = 0.265: mirror / low-detection second daughter (I-077) and the edge-net second daughter (I-078). The same logic covers insertion loosening (I-066/I-067). OLD VERDICT: refuted. Mirror: public +0.0001 central (P(< 0) 0.49), about 2.5 public missing-daughter cases, and the merged-blob geometry defeats the mirror. Edge-evidence: p(u->v) <= 0.52 (softmax over sources), an in-sample edge net, exp12 fork precision 0.19 < 0.265, and 0.4-1.2 evaluable public forks. Lowdet recovery: public -0.001..+0.001. Several of these skeptics also cited '0.003 LB noise'. WHAT CHANGED: (1) The 0.003-noise premise was overturned (deterministic kernels; a 0.001 public step is real), so 'a probe carries no signal' is too strong. (2) An x138 train lab now exists (exp60), which the schedule verdict said was missing. (3) Private (71%) break-even is 0.11-0.20 against 0.265 public, and private has ~2.4x the events. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The v3 skeptics had already priced in the private break-even (mirror private +0.0005 central, range -0.0005..+0.0016). The binding problems are unchanged. The detector confidence h, the DaughterNet p and the edge-net p are all in-sample on the exp60 clips (Addendum L5 labels the DaughterNet arms 'IN-SAMPLE UPPER BOUND'), which is the edge-filter trap. The public evaluable count is ~1-2.5 events. R4 needs +0.002 public for a fork-set changer, which is structurally unreachable here. R8 closes new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00, and section f/f2 leaves no 'private-leaning' final for an unmeasured rider. One structural note for the record: R4 read on public (J ~0.36) is biased against fork ADDITIONS that are private-positive, and biased toward REMOVALS. This is acceptable because K3's riders are removals with 0 expected TP loss.

findings.what: tempfuse (E7/C07/K4): the frame-t detection map is the mean of the pos-1 logits of (t-1, t) and the pos-0 logits of (t, t+1), with a per-frame top-K guard. OLD VERDICT: the value skeptic refuted it at +0.0008 central (-0.0005..+0.0015). Views are correlated (no temporal positional encoding, identity temporal block at full resolution), x138 readmit/gapfill already target the same subset, the V1284 head was trained on pos-1 peaks, and an out-of-sample analogue was only +0.0007. v3 kept it as optional 'cut first'. The curator then set the default to DROPPED unless a night round finds a strong reason before 26 Sep 12:00 UTC. Round 1 (M3) called it 'the one lever worth keeping only if node-neutral' and tightened its guard to +-0.3%. WHAT CHANGED: (1) The 12 h limit and ~4 h headroom do not matter: tempfuse costs ~0 GPU, and runtime was never its blocker. (2) Public/private split: every detection-map change on our LB was 0 or negative (Z-flip -0.003/-0.009, axis-flip -0.001, secondary weight -0.002, H2 closed). In-sample lab gains on these changes are large and embryo-specific, so a new embryo mix on private adds variance, not expected gain. (3) exp60 runs the detector on its own training clips, so there is no honest lab for a detection change. The v3 fix (LOEO test with friend_a_exp02_loeo20) needs friend A and has no owner. (4) The finals objective is P(private F1 > x138) first. F1's current margin over x138 is ~+0.001 public (the insertion), and adding a -0.0005..+0.0015 node-set changer raises variance around that margin. NEW VERDICT: STAYS DROPPED. Confirm the curator's default before 26 Sep 12:00 UTC so S6 stays empty or goes to the K3 retry.
